header.running_head: Hadhrat Abu Khaythama (RA) Forsakes the Luxuries of this world and Proceeds in the Path of Allaah

blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ commended him and prayed for him.[^1]

Hadhrat Sa'd bin Khaythama (RA) says, "I was unable to march with Rasulullaah ﷺ. When I entered my orchard, I saw a shelter sprinkled with water and my wife. I then said, 'This is not fair! Rasulullaah ﷺ is suffering in hot winds and heat while I am enjoying shade and luxury.' I then went to load my camel and took along some dates as my provisions. My wife called out, 'Where are you heading, O Abu Khaythama?' 'I am going to Rasulullaah ﷺ,' I replied." Narrating further, Hadhrat Abu Khaythama (RA) says, "I then left to find Rasulullaah ﷺ. On the road Umayr bin Wahab met me. I said to him, 'You are a brave man (and have nothing to fear being alone). I know where Rasulullaah ﷺ is and I am at fault (for not joining the army sooner). Do ride behind me so that I may meet Rasulullaah ﷺ alone.' Umayr did as I bid and as I set sight on the Muslim army, they also spotted me. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Let it be Abu Khaythama.' I approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'I had almost destroyed myself, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' After narrating my story to him, Rasulullaah ﷺ had good words to say and made du'aa for me."[^2]
The Grief of the Sahabah (RA) When they did not have the Ability to Go Out in the Path of Allaah or to Spend in the Path of Allaah
The Incident of Hadhrat Abu Layla (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mughaffal (RA)

Hadhrat Ibn Is'haaq says that the report reached him that Hadhrat Ibn Yaameen Nasri (RA) once met Hadhrat Abu Layla (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mughaffal (RA), both of whom were weeping. Hadhrat Ibn Yaameen (RA) asked, "What makes you two weep?" They replied, "We approached Rasulullaah ﷺ to provide transport for us (so that we could proceed in Jihaad) but we found nothing with him that we could use as transport. We also have nothing which could enable us to leave (in Jihaad) with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Ibn Yaameen (RA) then gave them his camel and some dates for the journey's provision. The two then left with Rasulullaah ﷺ.

A narration of Yunus bin Bukayr also from Ibn Is'haaq adds that another Sahabi by the name of Hadhrat Ulba bin Zaid (RA) (who also did not have the means to proceed in Jihaad) left at night and engaged in salaah for a considerable portion of the night. Thereafter, he started weeping and said, "O Allaah! You have issued the command to wage Jihaad and encouraged it. However, You have not given me the means with which to do it and have also not given to Your Rasulullaah ﷺ the means to provide transport for me. Now I wish to distribute

Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr and Moosa bin Uqba have also reported the story of Hadhrat Abu Khaythama (RA) in more detail. They mention that Hadhrat Abu Khaythama (RA) left for Tabook during autumn, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.5 Pg.7).
Tabraani, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.6 Pg.192). Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.193) has commented on the chain of narrators.
